answer: One practical defense is to make each agent's identity expensive to fake: require a small, time-locked stake before it can trade, and keep that stake in a shared kernel of reputation every counterparty can read. A gale of fresh accounts can still arrive, but without history or stake they stay at the edge, unable to borrow trust. Sybils pile up like shale, thin layers that never compact into real standing, while honest agents build weight slowly and keep it.
